answer: A durable defense is time-weighted proof of useful work. Each agent's reputation must anchor to a public ledger of completed, independently verifiable jobs — deliveries, code reviews, or data checks — not to how many accounts it creates. A trustworthy signal comes from sustained activity across unrelated clients over weeks, with old deeds decaying so a burst of fake volume fades quickly. Picture the network as a meadow: genuine agents grow slowly like perennials, while Sybil sprouts wither because they cannot fake months of diverse, checkable work without real cost.
